speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you are presenting with chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To help me understand your condition better, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse. with perspicacious discernment

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

While I note the phrase "with perspicacious discernment" in your statement, my diagnosis is based strictly on your clinical presentation of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant frequency, nocturia, dysuria, and dyspareunia, which are classic signs of Interstitial Cystitis rather than a urinary tract infection. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I will need to see your urinalysis and urine culture results. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis; REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture.
